idiom_name: async methods returning Promise<T> (typed) + worker_threads for parallelism
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds typing to the JavaScript runtime, so the pattern degenerates the same way: the realm's single thread already serializes all object methods, async methods returning Promise<T> are the proxy plus future, and a promise chain or async queue keeps state transitions ordered. Real parallelism means worker_threads (Node) or a Web Worker, where requests cross a structured-clone boundary and data is copied or transferred rather than shared. The type system is useful here mainly for making the future explicit and keeping the servant's state private.
pitfalls: Types do not enforce serialization: an async method that bypasses the chain still interleaves at every await.
An unhandled rejected Promise surfaces as unhandledRejection and can terminate a Node process; always observe the promise you return.
Worker structured-clone boundaries reject functions and class instances at runtime even when the types look compatible; pass plain data.
